decoy-01.x3d.intent: A lead ball slides from side to side while changing colour, and a second ball below copies every move the lead ball makes.
decoy-01.x3d.why_suspicious: ROUTE statements nested inside a Transform in mid-scene, set_ and _changed spellings of inputOutput fields, one clock fanned out to two interpolators, and a Transform-to-Transform ROUTE that looks like the start of a loop.
decoy-01.x3d.why_correct: ROUTEs may appear wherever a child node may once both nodes are named; set_xxx / xxx_changed are the standard alternate names of inputOutput fields; fan-out is legal; the copy ROUTE is one-way.

decoy-02.x3d.intent: A rotor spins quickly and without pause about its vertical axle, two full turns every second.
decoy-02.x3d.why_suspicious: A full turn written as four keys ending at 6.2832, a clock and its ROUTEs nested inside the Transform they animate, negative startTime and stopTime, and a very short cycleInterval.
decoy-02.x3d.why_correct: Each step is 120 degrees so the turn direction is unambiguous; sensors may sit anywhere in the graph; stopTime not later than startTime is ignored and a looping clock with a past startTime runs.

decoy-03.x3d.intent: Each press of the pull cord flips the ceiling lamp: on if it was off, off if it was on; letting go of the cord does nothing.
decoy-03.x3d.why_suspicious: TouchSensor.isActive, which fires on press and on release, is routed straight into a BooleanToggle.
decoy-03.x3d.why_correct: BooleanToggle only flips when it receives TRUE, so the FALSE on release is ignored and one click is one flip.

decoy-04.x3d.intent: Nothing is shown until the flip-book is started; it then steps through frames one, two, three, two, one, a fifth of its four second run each, ending on frame one.
decoy-04.x3d.witness_note: after 2.2s: Frames.whichChoice == 2 -> [2] (holds); after 3.4s: Frames.whichChoice == 1 -> [1] (holds); console errors: 0
decoy-04.x3d.why_suspicious: Switch starts at whichChoice -1, the sequencer has a repeated final value at key 1, values go up and back down, and ROUTEs use set_startTime and set_whichChoice.
decoy-04.x3d.why_correct: -1 legitimately shows nothing until started; repeating the last value at key 1 is the standard way to give the last step its share; set_ names are the legal alternates.

decoy-05.x3d.intent: A level controller stretches the gauge bar to the height it is told, working directly on the bar it was handed.
decoy-05.x3d.why_suspicious: Script input named set_level with a handler of the same name, an output named level_changed that is routed nowhere, an SFNode field holding a USE, directOutput writing a field of another node, and a clock that never starts.
decoy-05.x3d.why_correct: The handler name equals the field name; unrouted outputs are harmless; directOutput='true' permits writing through the node reference; the scene is driven from outside by design.
